original_abstract: Financial fraud detection and borrower delinquency assessment involve different targets but share the need for careful evaluation under class imbalance. FraudShield integrates two independent Random Forest pipelines within an authenticated application. This study reports preserved experiments comparing weighted and unweighted forests with a constant-prior baseline. IEEE-CIS uses chronological 70/15/15 partitions, while Give Me Some Credit uses stratified random partitions in the same proportions. Forests and decision thresholds are selected using validation F1. The selected unweighted models use 431 and 10 inputs, with thresholds of 0.21 and 0.23. Saved holdout results give fraud precision 0.343373, recall 0.406747 and F1 0.372383 on 88,581 transactions; credit precision is 0.407090, recall 0.473404 and F1 0.437750 on 22,500 borrowers. The unweighted fraud forest wins validation F1, but its weighted comparator achieves higher holdout F1, 0.444087. This reversal is retained rather than used for retrospective model selection. Artifact inspection supports common fitted preprocessing, although exact historical training-row identity for the reused weighted fraud model remains unproven. Trapezoidal precision–recall area and Average Precision are reported separately. The empirical contribution is a task-specific candidate-and-operating-point comparison that exposes a validation-to-holdout ordering reversal without test-based reselection. Application integration is documented at source level; live end-to-end verification is a prospective systems question, outside the answered research questions. The study does not establish a new detection method, calibrated financial risk, fused prediction or drift adaptation.
